newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says US must keep international commitments.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says US must keep international commitments.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Tuesday that the United States must keep its commitments to the United Nations and international financial institutions, saying "we cannot lead with other people's money."

The United States is the world's largest and richest economy, yet it has the largest arrears to the United Nations, and has the lion's share of arrears to multilateral development banks and the Global Environment Fund, Rubin said in prepared remarks to a Senate subcommittee.

"We must fully commit to our foreign affairs budget, which pays for the United Nations, bilateral assistance programs and the international financial institutions -- the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund and the regional development banks," Rubin said. He said all this together accounted for less than one percent of the U.S. federal budget.

"This year is critical," Rubin said. "If we do not meet our commitments, we will put at risk our leadership in these institutions and thereby our ability to shape policy with respect to developing countries," he said.
"This risks affecting foreign policy priorities in places from Bosnia to the former Soviet Union to Africa," Rubin said. "We cannot lead with other people's money."
The United States is behind in its payments to multilateral development banks by $862 million, Rubin said.

He said the Clinton administration's budget request of $1.6 billion for multilateral development banks includes over $300 million to partially pay down those arrears, with the remainder going to meet annual commitments. Meanwhile the administration has achieved a 40 percent reduction in future U.S. obligations to the these banks, he said.
